answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, so influence reaches only vertices connected by sufficiently supported paths. A sybil cluster with few external attestations has low conductance: its sparse cut limits probability flow to honest nodes and, under normalized voting and capped per-path influence, bounds its aggregate voting weight. A quartz-weighted edge thread may encode attestations; the kernel of the walk operator can reveal disconnected collusion rather than grant it reach.
